q: Which departments is the model losing to the naive baseline, and why might that be?
answer:
Five of seven departments have negative FVA: HOUSEHOLD_1 (-9.4pp), HOUSEHOLD_2 (-7.6pp), FOODS_1 (-7.3pp), FOODS_3 (-7.0pp), and marginally FOODS_2 (-0.9pp). Only HOBBIES_2 (+10.6pp) and HOBBIES_1 (+2.8pp) beat the baseline, and pooled FVA is -5.7pp (model 79.5% vs naive 85.2%).

Likely reason: the losers are exactly where the seasonal-naive baseline is already very strong — HOUSEHOLD_1 87.8%, FOODS_3 87.1%, HOUSEHOLD_2 86.6% naive accuracy — i.e. stable, strongly weekly-seasonal demand that last week's same weekday already captures, leaving little headroom. Conversely the model wins where the naive is weak and noisy (HOBBIES_2 naive 54.9%). Bias is not the main driver: the biggest loser HOUSEHOLD_1 is only +4.1% biased and FOODS_3 only -0.7%, so the loss is dispersion/day-to-day error, not systematic over- or under-forecasting. Note this is an interpretation of the pattern, not something the tools measure directly. It matters commercially because FOODS_3 (615,655 units) and HOUSEHOLD_1 (163,737 units) are the two largest departments.

q: Since Elastic Net's WAPE is 4x better than Prophet's, should we switch all departments to Elastic Net?
answer: The premise doesn't hold. Prophet's WAPE is measured on daily forecasts, Elastic Net's on monthly aggregates; monthly aggregation cancels day-to-day noise, so the two numbers are not comparable head-to-head and the gap is not a 4x quality advantage. Also, even taken at face value, Elastic Net is not better everywhere: in HOBBIES_2 its monthly WAPE is 58.96% vs Prophet's 34.32% daily. Examples of the reported pairs (daily Prophet / monthly Elastic Net): FOODS_3 19.81 / 4.86, HOUSEHOLD_1 21.56 / 3.26, HOBBIES_1 18.57 / 4.32, FOODS_2 20.55 / 5.31, FOODS_1 24.99 / 6.96, HOUSEHOLD_2 20.94 / 8.99. So no blanket switch: if you need daily replenishment forecasts, a monthly-aggregate model doesn't answer the same question. A like-for-like test at the same granularity would be needed, and that number isn't in this backtest. Separately, note the current planning model is already behind the seasonal-naive baseline overall (79.5% vs 85.2% accuracy, FVA -5.7pp, only 2 of 7 departments beating naive), so the baseline is the benchmark any candidate model must clear.
